stem: A patient presents with a pH of 7.5, pCO2 of 25, pO2 of 60, HCO2 is 24 and base deficit is > 2.5. What is the acid base abnormality?
expl: pH 7.5 = alkalemia; PCO₂ 25 is low (primary respiratory) with normal HCO₃ 24 → acute respiratory alkalosis (e.g. hyperventilation from hypoxia, PO₂ 60).

stem: A 65-year-old male in the ICU for septic shock develops sudden abdominal pain, distension, and mild lactic acidosis. He is hemodynamically unstable. What is the most likely diagnosis?
expl: Septic shock on vasopressors + abdominal pain, distension and lactic acidosis = non-occlusive mesenteric ischaemia (low-flow splanchnic vasoconstriction).

why.A: Sudden pain in AF/embolic source, out of proportion.

stem: high ileostomy output cause what?
expl: Ileostomy/small-bowel fluid is rich in bicarbonate → loss → normal-anion-gap (hyperchloremic) metabolic acidosis.

stem: “Scenario suggesting hypocalcemia”, ECG shows prolonged QT interval, which of the following is the treatment?
expl: Hypocalcemia prolongs the QT; treat with IV calcium gluconate.

stem: patient Underwent Multiple laparotomy. Then become with enterocutaneous fistula What electrolytes imbalance is expected:-
expl: Enterocutaneous (small-bowel) fistula loses bicarbonate-rich fluid → metabolic acidosis.

stem: Which of the following is known as a “ triad for death”?
expl: The lethal triad of trauma: acidosis, hypothermia and coagulopathy — each worsens the others; damage-control surgery aims to break it.

stem: 65 year old male post open cholecystectomy, can’t tolerate food on continuous NGT suction, which of the following abnormalities is expected to be in this pt?
srcNote: (Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient)
expl: Continuous NG suction removes gastric HCl → metabolic alkalosis (with hypokalemia and hypochloremia).

stem: 52 y/o male patient was brought to emergency department unconscious after falling from a bridge about 6 meters high. His initial observations showed: T: 36.2 0C, BP: 80/50 mmHg ... What is the most accurate indicator of inadequate tissue perfusion in this patient?
srcNote: (Trauma)
expl: Lactate reflects anaerobic metabolism → the most accurate marker of inadequate tissue perfusion.

stem: You obtained arterial blood gas, and these are the labs: PH: 7.2, HCO3: 15, HCO2: 55, Na: 132, Cl: 95. Which of the following is the value of the anion gap?
srcNote: ( fluids and acids base ,electrolytes imbalance )

stem: Which of the following is a normal anion gap metabolic acidosis?
srcNote: (Principles of Fluids and Electrolytes Balance in Surgical Patients)
expl: Small-bowel fistula loses bicarbonate → normal-AG metabolic acidosis. Alcohol, aspirin and DKA cause high-AG acidosis.

stem: Which of the following is true about metabolic alkalosis?

opts.t: Loss of fixed acid or gain in bicarbonate

srcNote: (Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient)
expl: Metabolic alkalosis = loss of non-volatile (fixed) acid or gain of HCO₃; compensation is HYPOventilation.

stem: Most common fluid problem in surgical patients
srcNote: (Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient)
expl: Extracellular volume deficit (hypovolemia) is the most common fluid disorder in surgical patients.

why.B: Common, but ECF loss is keyed.

stem: A 45-year-old man presented to the hospital with acute left leg ischemia secondary to trauma After revascularization, the patient should be observed for potential complication. Which complication is most likely to occur secondary to reperfusion syndrome?
expl: Reperfusion of an ischaemic limb washes potassium, lactic acid and myoglobin from dead muscle into the circulation → hyperkalaemia (arrhythmias), metabolic acidosis, myoglobinuric renal failure, plus compartment syndrome. (The source writes "Ans. A".)

stem: A 25-year-old man who underwent sleeve gastrectomy for morbid obesity. 7 days ago he developed gastric fistula with output of 250 ml/day. Which of the following is the most frequently associated with this condition?
srcNote: (Principles of Fluids and Electrolytes Balance in Surgical Patients)
expl: Gastric juice is rich in HCl and K⁺ → a gastric fistula causes hypokalemia (with hypochloremic alkalosis).

why.A: Urine K⁺ may be high in alkalosis, but hypokalemia is keyed.

stem: Pt underwent gastric sleeve, developed gastric fistula. What abnormality will be found?
srcNote: (Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient)
expl: Gastric fluid is rich in HCl and K⁺ → a gastric fistula causes hypokalemia (with hypochloremic alkalosis).

why.D: Urine K⁺ may rise in alkalosis but hypokalemia is keyed.

stem: A labourer is brought to the emergency department unconscious after falling from a bridge about 6 meters’ height. The patient received 2 liters of bolus crystalloid intravenous fluid. His initial vitals are: BP:100/40, HR: 110/min, RR 22/min, T: 36.2 C Which of the following is the most accurate indicator of adequacy of fluid replacement?
srcNote: (Principles of Fluids and Electrolytes Balance in Surgical Patients)
expl: Urine output (≥0.5 ml/kg/h adult) is the best bedside indicator of adequate resuscitation/end-organ perfusion.

why.A: Lactate shows perfusion but lags behind.

stem: A 38-year-old man was brought to the ER after he was involved in MVA, on arrival, he was agitated, BP=90/56 mmHg, HR=107b/m, tenderness with reduced air entry over the right side of the chest and normal abdominal examination. The arterial ABG result are listed below: pH = 7.3 HCO3 = 18 PaCO2 = 52 SaO2= 80 Which of the following is the appropriate next step?
srcNote: (Trauma) in case of respiratory distress secondary to pneumothorax, breathing takes priority over airway in the initial trauma survey. - Uptodate Source note (433 A Q2): unstable patients with traumatic pneumothorax: needle thoracostomy (failed?) > finger thoracostomy > (consider chest tube for bilateral pneumothorax , patient requires mechanical ventilation or doesn’t meet pneumothorax stability criteria) - AMBOSS
expl: Trauma, agitation, hypotension, reduced air entry and tenderness on one side with respiratory acidosis and low saturation = tension pneumothorax → immediate needle decompression (breathing problem threatening life; don't wait for X-ray). Source note: unstable traumatic pneumothorax → needle (or finger) thoracostomy, then chest tube.

why.A: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis — no X-ray first.
why.B: Definitive, but decompression comes first in the unstable patient.
why.C: Intubation with positive pressure worsens a tension pneumothorax.

stem: In patients with raised ICP secondary to severe traumatic brain injury, hyperventilation may be considered as a temporary procedure to reduce the ICP. When using this modality profound hypocarbia must be avoided to prevent which of the following?

opts.t: Shift of oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve to left.
Respiratory acidosis leading to secondary cerebral edema.

srcNote: , (Principles of Fluids and Electrolytes Balance in Surgical Patients) Davidson P:458
expl: Hypocarbia causes cerebral vasoconstriction → ICP falls but cerebral ischemia follows if PCO₂ drops too far.

why.C: True but not the main danger.

stem: A 20-year old woman presents with general weakness and vomiting. Her work up showed: blood glucose level of 30mmol/l, pH 7.05, PCO2 20, HCO3 11, Na 126, K 3.3, Cl 90. Which of the following is the anion gap for this patient?
srcNote: (Principles of Fluids and Electrolytes Balance in Surgical Patients)

stem: 55-year-old woman is known to have chronic duodenal ulcer, presented to the emergency department with a history of frequent vomiting of old food for two weeks. On examination she had a distended upper abdomen and normal abdominal sound. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy showed obstructed pylorus due to chronic peptic ulcer disease. Which of the following is electrolyte and acid-base balance abnormality?
srcNote: (Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient)
expl: Gastric outlet obstruction with vomiting → loss of HCl → hypochloremic hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.

why.A: Urine K⁺ may be high, but the key disturbance is alkalosis.

stem: Early morning headache is a sign of increased intracranial pressure. What is the mechanism underlying this headache?
expl: During sleep, ventilation falls → PaCO₂ rises → cerebral vasodilation → more intracranial blood volume → ICP rises further in a patient with reduced compliance → early-morning headache (with vomiting).

stem: A 32y\o man, 7 days post right hemicolectomy with NGT in situ, found in arterial blood gases to have PH 7.5 and high bicarbonate level. Which of the following is possible associated abnormalities?
expl: NG drainage → metabolic alkalosis (pH 7.5, high HCO₃) associated with hypokalemia (and hypochloremia, paradoxical aciduria).

stem: A 47-year-old lady underwent small bowel resection with anastomosis, then she developed high output small bowel fistula ( 700ml/day ) Which of the following is the expected electrolyte/metabolic abnormality?
srcNote: (Principles of Fluids and Electrolytes Balance in Surgical Patients)
expl: High-output small-bowel fistula loses HCO₃-rich fluid → metabolic acidosis.

stem: Which of the following is a cause of high anion gap metabolic acidosis?
srcNote: , shock causes lactic acidosis Source note (431 A Q16): (severe hemorrhage leading to hypovolemic shock � lactic acidosis)
expl: Hemorrhagic shock → tissue hypoperfusion → lactic acidosis (high anion gap). Diarrhea and fistulas give normal-AG acidosis.

stem: You obtained arterial blood gas, and these are the labs: Cl 95, Na 132 HCO3 8 Pco2 45 Which of the following is the value of the anion gap?
srcNote: NA-(CL+HCO3)

stem: 48 y\o man known to have chronic prepyloric peptic ulcer, presented to ER with a history of frequent vomiting. Which of the following acid-base balance this patient may have?
srcNote: (Principles of Fluids and Electrolytes Balance in Surgical Patients)
expl: Pyloric obstruction with vomiting → loss of HCl → metabolic alkalosis.

stem: A 55 y\o man, 2nd day post-total gastrectomy with excessive opiate administration found in arterial blood gas to have PH 7.3. He was febrile with normal pulse and blood pressure. Which of the following is the possible associated electrolyte and acid-base abnormality?
srcNote: ( Principles of Fluids and Electrolytes Balance in Surgical Patients ) resp depression due to opiate use Source note (429 F Q60): Opiate causes depression of the respiratory centre and hence an increase in PaCO2 which cause respiratory acidosis.
expl: Excess opiates → respiratory depression → CO₂ retention → respiratory acidosis (high PaCO₂).

stem: 48 y\o man known to have chronic prepyloric peptic ulcer, presented to ER with a history of frequent vomiting since 4 days. On examination he was dehydrated. Upper GI endoscopy showed gastric outlet obstruction. Which of the following acid-base balance this patient may have?
srcNote: (Principles of Fluids and Electrolytes Balance in Surgical Patients)
expl: Gastric outlet obstruction → loss of HCl → metabolic alkalosis with hypokalemia.

stem: A 32 y/o man victim of motor vehicle accident with massive intra-abdominal bleeding. Received 10 units of packed red blood cells within 12 hours. Which of the following is the most common complication this patient may have?
srcNote: (Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient)
expl: Stored blood leaks K⁺ from lysed cells → hyperkalemia after massive transfusion (also citrate toxicity/hypocalcemia, hypothermia, coagulopathy).

why.B: Acidosis early (alkalosis later from citrate metabolism).

stem: A 46 y/o diabetic man admitted through emergency department with diagnosis of ascending cholangitis. He was started on therapeutic course of intravenous amoxicillin, metronidazole and gentamicin. Three days later the serum urea and creatinine steadily elevated. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step in management?
srcNote: ( Pre-operative assessment )
expl: Gentamicin is nephrotoxic; a rising creatinine means stop it (and switch to a non-nephrotoxic agent).

stem: You obtained arterial blood gas, and these are the labs: Cl 95, Na 132 HCO3 15 Pco2 45 Which of the following is the value of the anion gap?
srcNote: ( Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient ) AG=Na-(cl+hco3)

stem: What can cause Normal AG metabolic Acidosis?
srcNote: ( Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient ) (Hyperchloremic acidosis is a form of metabolic acidosis associated with normal AG but is not a cause)
expl: Renal tubular acidosis causes normal-AG (hyperchloremic) acidosis; "hyperchloremic acidosis" describes the result, not a cause.

stem: A 64 y/o man with history of emphysema was admitted with hematemesis. The bleeding ceased after admission but the patient became confused and agitated. The arterial blood gas was as following: pH: 7.23, PO2: 42 mmHg, PCO2: 75 mmHg.Which of the following is the most appropriate therapy?

opts.t: Correct hypoxemia with high flow O2.

srcNote: ( Trauma ) Source note (429 F Q18): primary survey
expl: Acute-on-chronic hypercapnic respiratory failure (pH 7.23, PCO₂ 75) with confusion → intubation and ventilation.

why.C: High-flow O₂ can worsen hypercapnia in COPD.

stem: A 17 y/o male was involved in a road traffic accident, brought to the emergency department with closed head injury and multiple other injuries. During resuscitation in the emergency room he received 2 litters of crystalloids and 3 units of packed red blood cells. After he was stabilized he moved to the ICU. His electrolytes showed Na: 135 mmol/l, Cl: 115 mmol/l and HCO3 13 (Low). What is the most appropriate fluid resuscitation at this stage?
srcNote: ( Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient )
expl: After 2 L of NS-type crystalloid he has hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis (Cl 115, HCO₃ 13). Further resuscitation should use a balanced solution (Ringer's lactate), not more saline.

stem: 56 y\o man known to have chronic renal failure found to have serum potassium of 6.9 meq\dl. Which of the following is an appropriate emergency treatment?
srcNote: (Principles of fluids and electrolytes balance in surgical patient) . To protect the heart
expl: Hyperkalemia emergency → calcium (chloride or gluconate) to stabilize the myocardium.

stem: Emphysema patient came with hematemesis, found to have Low PH, co2 high, o2 low what will u do?
srcNote: (Trauma), primary survey
expl: Source key D: correct hypoxia with high oxygen (primary survey). The 430 version of the same scenario keyed intubation — with pH low, PCO₂ high and confusion, ventilation is needed.

stem: complication of Massive transfusion:
expl: Massive transfusion → citrate toxicity (hypocalcemia), hypothermia, hyperkalemia, coagulopathy.
